work.title: Move an Issue's Project status only when a run attacks the Work
work.description: The Project projection derives an Issue's status from the stage the Work is ready for, so the board advertises a stage no agent has started: complete Plan and the Issue jumps to Review while it only waits. The board should report activity, not readiness. A Work no run has attacked stays Backlog; a live run shows its stage; a Work waiting between runs keeps the stage last attacked; a terminal Work shows Done. Status changes remain reconciliation — a sync with no new run edits nothing.
acceptance: Starting a stage run moves the Work's Issue to that stage's Project status on the next sync
A Work waiting between stages keeps the status of the stage last attacked instead of advertising the stage it is ready for
A Work no run has ever attacked projects as Backlog, even one ready for Plan
A terminal Work still projects Done, and a sync with no new run edits no status

result.handoff:
# Plan: Move an Issue's Project status only when a run attacks the Work (INIT-2.3)

## Finding (P1)
snapshotOf (src/application/publication.ts:44-53) derives Project Status as `PROJECT_STATUS_BY_STAGE[manifest.workflow.stage]` whenever any attempt exists. workflow.stage is the stage the Work is *ready for*, so completing Plan moves the board to Review while the Work only waits — the board reports readiness, not activity. Two existing tests pin that wrong behavior and must flip: publication.test.ts:368 (expects "Review" after plan completes) and publication.test.ts:436 (same in the recovery scenario). The projection E2E asserts Plan/Verify/Done only immediately after the corresponding stage was attacked (projection-e2e.mjs:179, 193, 211), so it passes unchanged under the new rule.

## Product files Build touches
1. src/application/publication.ts — the only production change, one line inside snapshotOf: derive the status from the latest attempt's stage instead of workflow.stage.
2. src/test/publication.test.ts — update two expectations, add two tests.

## The rule (P2)
```
completion !== null        -> "Done"
no attempts                -> "Backlog"
otherwise                  -> PROJECT_STATUS_BY_STAGE[latestAttempt.stage]
```
The latest attempt's stage is exactly "the stage last attacked":
- A live run (attempt active) shows its stage — acceptance 1.
- A completed run leaves its stage up while the Work waits for the next one — acceptance 2.
- A returned attempt still shows the stage that was attacked (e.g. review returns to plan: the board keeps Review until a new run starts), because the status moved when that attack began and nothing newer happened. Tests pin this edge.
- Never attacked stays Backlog — acceptance 3, existing assertion at publication.test.ts:87.
- Terminal shows Done and the derivation is stable across syncs with no new run, so the board value never moves — acceptance 4.

No new core helper: the derivation stays in snapshotOf where it already lived — the smallest change that carries the semantics.

## Tests (P3)
1. Update publication.test.ts:368 — after plan completes, the board shows "Plan" (waiting keeps the last-attacked stage), not "Review".
2. Update publication.test.ts:436 — the recovery scenario expects "Plan" for the same reason.
3. New: live run — app.works.start("review", workId, ...) without completing, then reconcile; the board shows "Review" while the run is open (acceptance 1).
4. New: stability — after a Work is terminal, a repeated reconcile reports the same status and the board value does not move (acceptance 4).
5. Existing: Backlog for a never-attacked Work (line 87) and Done at terminal (lines 374, 396) stay green.

## Acceptance coverage
1. Starting a run moves the status — latest-attempt derivation + test 3.
2. Waiting between stages keeps the last-attacked stage — same derivation + tests 1–2.
3. Never attacked projects Backlog — unchanged branch + existing test.
4. Terminal stays Done, no status movement without a new run — unchanged Done branch + test 4.

## Verification for Build
npm run verify (typecheck, unit tests, smoke, --help).

## Non-goals
No change to the E2E scenario, the gh-projects adapter (its idempotent item-edit is fine — the observable status does not move), Issue creation timing, milestones, or outcome mapping.

traces.message: snapshotOf (publication.ts:44-53) derives Project Status from manifest.workflow.stage — the stage the Work is ready for — so completing Plan moves the board to Review while the Work only waits. Two existing tests pin that readiness behavior and must flip: publication.test.ts:368 expects "Review" after plan completes, line 436 likewise. The projection E2E only asserts statuses immediately after a stage was attacked (Plan line 179, Verify line 193, Done line 211), so it survives the rule unchanged.

The rule is a one-line change inside snapshotOf: derive from the latest attempt's stage instead of workflow.stage. Done when terminal, Backlog when there is no attempt, otherwise the stage of the last attempt — which is exactly "the stage last attacked": an active run shows its stage, a completed run leaves its stage up while the Work waits, and a returned attempt still shows the stage that was attacked. No new core helper: the derivation stays where it already lived, and tests pin the semantics including the return edge.

Tests: update the two readiness expectations (publication.test.ts:368 and :436) from "Review" to "Plan" — that flip is the behavior change; add a live-run test using app.works.start without complete so the board shows the attacked stage while the run is open; keep the existing Backlog and Done assertions and add a re-sync-with-no-new-run assertion that the board value does not move. No E2E change.

result.handoff:
# Build: INIT-2.3

## Changed files (product)
- src/application/publication.ts — `snapshotOf` now uses `latest.stage` instead of `manifest.workflow.stage`. A comment captures the rule: the board reports activity, not readiness.
- src/test/publication.test.ts — two existing tests updated to expect "Plan" after Plan completes (the board keeps the last-attacked stage while waiting); two new tests: a live Review run shows "Review" on the next sync, and a terminal Work's second sync writes the same Done/Accepted value back so the board value does not move.

## Validation
- `npm run verify` green: typecheck, 255/255 unit tests (2 new + 2 updated), smoke, --help.

## Commits
- f6982bb INIT-2.3-move-an-issue-s-project-status-only-when-a-run-a: Move an Issue's Project status only when a run attacks the Work (product)
- 3591774 codepatrol(INIT-2.3-move-an-issue-s-project-status-only-when-a-run-a): manifest projection (state update for the active Build run)

## Candidate
- The product commit `f6982bb` carries every code and test change. The branch head `3591774` is the manifest projection that the Build run wrote on its way to completion. Both are clean and reproducible from `06f9236`.

## Acceptance
1. Starting a run moves the status to that stage on the next sync — latest-attempt derivation + new live-run test.
2. A Work waiting between stages keeps the last-attacked stage — same derivation + two updated tests.
3. A Work no run has ever attacked projects as Backlog — unchanged branch + existing test at publication.test.ts:87.
4. A terminal Work still projects Done, and a sync with no new run edits no status — unchanged Done branch + new stability test.
